blocks.html_en:
Running a full LLM to actuate a robot is way too heavy, the minimum latency they can get down to is probably 1-2 seconds even with powerful GPUs, which is not very useful for practical robotics applications.

Machine vision should definitely be handled by ML, but motion actuation should be relegated in the realm of traditional PID style linear/nonlinear control. Again, the tech is cool, but the practical usefulness of using a full LLM as a controller will probably run into hardware limitations.

blocks.html_en:
On latency: that is true now but likely false in the near future. There is so much potential left over for optimizing inference further.

On PID: the field has been stuck trying to do analytical/optimization-based control for decades, and end-to-end control has shown incredible performance (e.g., SoTA cost of transport in legged locomotion) and robustness (e.g., not falling over when stepping on a pile of leaves) - while being far scalable (in terms of how fast it is to get a new robot up and running). Which is not to say it's perfect but it seems like it's a step in the right direction.

Better yet, companies like Physical Intelligence are doing good with hierarchical ("fast-slow") architecture to address both the intelligence and latency fronts.

sentences.en: On latency: that is true now but likely false in the near future.
sentences.zh: 关于延迟：现在这是正确的，但在不久的将来可能是错误的。

sentences.zh: 进一步优化推理还有很大的潜力。关于 PID：数十年来，该领域一直致力于基于分析/优化的控制，而端到端控制已经显示出令人难以置信的性能（例如，腿式运动的 SoTA 运输成本）和鲁棒性（例如，踩在一堆树叶上时不会摔倒），同时具有很大的可扩展性（就启动和运行新机器人的速度而言）。

sentences.en: Which is not to say it's perfect but it seems like it's a step in the right direction.Better yet, companies like Physical Intelligence are doing good with hierarchical ("fast-slow") architecture to address both the intelligence and latency fronts.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说它是完美的，但它似乎是朝着正确方向迈出的一步。更好的是，像 Physical Intelligence 这样的公司正在利用分层（“快-慢”）架构来解决智能和延迟方面的问题。

sentences.en: There is so much potential left over for optimizing inference further.On PID: the field has been stuck trying to do analytical/optimization-based control for decades, and end-to-end control has shown incredible performance (e.g., SoTA cost of transport in legged locomotion) and robustness (e.g., not falling over when stepping on a pile of leaves) - while being far scalable (in terms of how fast it is to get a new robot up and running).

10Hz is still a 0.1s of latency, which doesn't seem like a lot until you realize that an Arduino typically runs at 16 Mhz, which is literally a million times faster than running a full LLM.

So, yeah, for complex reasoning and sensory processing, LLMs are the correct choice, and Gemini is especially strong at spatial reasoning over ChatGPT/Claude. But for actual motion/actuation? LLMs are the wrong tool for the job, probably easier to have LLMs program a reusable workflow in a script for repeated tasks instead of invoking LLMs after the first time.

blocks.html_en:
Big humanoid robots are expensive, the actuators still suck, and the control problems are hard. Their big advantage is that they can occupy human-shaped spaces, but struggle to do anything useful.

Not to say we won't get humanoid robots eventually, but I think there's probably some low hanging fruit for people to make some other kinds of solutions. Specialized robots for industrial environment, well-thought out appliances for the home.

It would be a bit surprising if the progression was Roomba -> humanoid robot.

A lot of these household tasks could be automated without the need for humanoid robots. Roombas can clean your floor, automated rubbish disposal can be integrated into houses and flats, grocery delivery and storage could be done via an automated intake, cataloguing, and storage system. Humanoids are just creepy and you can't really trust them.

Could you sleep easily knowing that you have one in your house? What if you oppose the political views of its creators?

Humanoids are a useful form factor because the already-built human world is, definitionally, built for humanoids.

My point is that a generalist-humanoid robot can be used for nefarious purposes more easily than a specialised robot like a Roomba. A humanoid robot could, in an extreme case, perform a civil arrest or prevent you from leaving your house until the police arrives. Ultimately it's our decision to make.

1. Do we want to be governed by machines?

2. Do we want to relinquish our freedoms to the whims of corporations?

blocks.html_en:
You are being far too kind. A primate's body shape may be optimal for life in the trees, but it sure isn't optimal for any of the industrial or household tasks we want a robot to do. There are millions of robots around the world doing useful things, from vacuuming houses to assembling iPhones and playing table tennis. None of them look remotely like a human.

If an article features a humanoid robot it's sure sign its a PR fluff piece. This one looks to be a recruitment ad. Tesla's Optimus is being used to pump some sort of investment scam. God knows China's humanoid marathon is about. Whatever it is, it isn't getting from A to B quickly and efficiently.

blocks.html_en:
I actually like Tau's videos a lot better than Google's. An agile robot getting out of a car carrying a tote is actually novel and difficult and useful. In contrast, what Google is showing here is mostly glorified pick and place with low success rates on a needlessly complex robot and a voice LLM slapped on top to pre-announce its moves like an anime character, with fancy video editing and bubbly music to distract you from how slow it is.

Sure Tau is teleoperated, but teleoperating an agile movement like that is actually really hard to get right and still involves AI to keep the robot balanced. Tau is a lot closer to real deployment than Google, and when it performs useful tasks it is simultaneously collecting the data to eventually automate those tasks.

sentences.zh: 事实上，我比 Google 的视频更喜欢 Tau 的视频。

sentences.en: An agile robot getting out of a car carrying a tote is actually novel and difficult and useful.
sentences.zh: 一个敏捷的机器人带着手提包从车里走出来实际上是新颖的、困难的和有用的。

sentences.en: In contrast, what Google is showing here is mostly glorified pick and place with low success rates on a needlessly complex robot and a voice LLM slapped on top to pre-announce its moves like an anime character, with fancy video editing and bubbly music to distract you from how slow it is.Sure Tau is teleoperated, but teleoperating an agile movement like that is actually really hard to get right and still involves AI to keep the robot balanced.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，谷歌在这里展示的主要是美化的拾取和放置，在一个不必要的复杂机器人上成功率很低，还有一个声音法学硕士在上面像动漫角色一样预先宣布它的动作，用花哨的视频编辑和活泼的音乐来分散你对它有多慢的注意力。当然，Tau 是远程操作的，但远程操作这样的敏捷动作实际上很难做到正确，并且仍然需要人工智能来保持机器人平衡。

sentences.en: Tau is a lot closer to real deployment than Google, and when it performs useful tasks it is simultaneously collecting the data to eventually automate those tasks.
sentences.zh: Tau 比 Google 更接近实际部署，当它执行有用的任务时，它会同时收集数据以最终自动化这些任务。

Sure Tau is teleoperated, but teleoperating an agile movement like that is actually really hard to get right and still involves AI to keep the robot balanced. Tau is a lot closer to real deployment than Google, and when it performs useful tasks it is simultaneously collecting the data to eventually automate those tasks.

I think the biggest snag with home robots will be that if it is strong enough to install your air conditioners, it's strong enough to break your ribs.

So the robots will need to be weak, so even weak people can overpower it. But then it loses a ton of it's most promising abilities.

I don't mean this like a "rogue robot" situation. I mean it like the robot gets confused, or someone sees a walking $10M lawsuit in their home.

blocks.html_en:
I think that people will argue around that. Self-driving cars are already strong enough to kill people and even if you only made the robot strong enough to lift 15 pounds of weight, that's probably strong enough to slit someone's throat with a kitchen knife while they sleep... There probably isn't a level of strength that's weak enough to be completely safe but strong enough to be useful.

So at some point you have to trust that the tech is safe. Both in terms of "robot won't go off the rails", but also in terms of hostile actors can't remotely take over your robot while you sleep.

In terms of sleeping, personally, I would like for the law to mandate that robots must have a physical off switch, in a very visible location, that physically disconnects power. The switch should be illuminated while in the ON position. What makes me a bit pessimistic there is that we don't even have laws to mandate webcam indicator lights (e.g. a very tiny red LED) must be ON in hardware.

blocks.html_en:
Humanoid robots can be dropped in wherever human labor is currently used.

That makes them extremely easy to sell to industry. This unlocks, in principle, a large chunk of the potential untapped industrial automation market that still relies on human labor because the ROI of redesigning production lines didn't make sense.

blocks.html_en:
I don't think it's the dream, I think it's the cynical market-driven logic.

Automation has been rolling out for a long while now, and most of the low-hanging fruit of things that can easily be redesigned in a cost-effective way has been dealt with already. The role of these robots is to address all of the stuff that would have been automated by now if they could have.

Why do we want to add more bodies on a finite plane of existence with an infinitely-expanding base (humans)?

We have a finite plane of existence (Earth), with an infinitely-expanding consumer base (humans), and we want to add robotic competition to that finite plane of existence? The data center AI is more appealing (I guess) since it doesn't compete literally shoulder-to-shoulder with me. Why do we want dexterous robots when we have humans?

blocks.html_en:
It's a load of bollocks, and always was.

Modern robotics is, at its core, not a hardware problem. It's an AI problem. We have plenty of headroom in the hardware - what we don't have is an AI good enough to utilize it. We don't know the practical limits of current hardware because we can't make a robot AI that would make the hardware a meaningful bottleneck.

Today's robots don't fail at tasks because they have poor fingers. They fail because they don't know how to perform those tasks. If you put an effort into solving that? You get demos like: Gemini Robotics 2 tying a garbage bag. Take one long look at that and think of manual dexterity.

Human body is crude and suboptimal in a thousands different ways, and all of it is salvaged by advanced intelligence.

sentences.zh: 这是一派胡言，而且一直都是。现代机器人技术的核心不是硬件问题。

sentences.en: It's an AI problem.
sentences.zh: 这是一个人工智能问题。

sentences.en: We have plenty of headroom in the hardware - what we don't have is an AI good enough to utilize it.
sentences.zh: 我们在硬件上有足够的空间——但我们没有足够好的人工智能来利用它。

sentences.en: We don't know the practical limits of current hardware because we can't make a robot AI that would make the hardware a meaningful bottleneck.Today's robots don't fail at tasks because they have poor fingers.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道当前硬件的实际限制，因为我们无法制造出使硬件成为有意义的瓶颈的机器人人工智能。今天的机器人不会因为手指不好而在任务中失败。

sentences.en: They fail because they don't know how to perform those tasks.
sentences.zh: 他们失败是因为他们不知道如何执行这些任务。

sentences.en: If you put an effort into solving that?
sentences.zh: 如果你努力解决这个问题？

sentences.en: You get demos like: Gemini Robotics 2 tying a garbage bag.
sentences.zh: 您会得到类似这样的演示：Gemini Robotics 2 系垃圾袋。

blocks.html_en:
It's a load of bollocks, and always was.

Modern robotics is, at its core, not a hardware problem. It's an AI problem. We have plenty of headroom in the hardware - what we don't have is an AI good enough to utilize it. We don't know the practical limits of current hardware because we can't make a robot AI that would make the hardware a meaningful bottleneck.

Today's robots don't fail at tasks because they have poor fingers. They fail because they don't know how to perform those tasks. If you put an effort into solving that? You get demos like: Gemini Robotics 2 tying a garbage bag. Take one long look at that and think of manual dexterity.

Human body is crude and suboptimal in a thousands different ways, and all of it is salvaged by advanced intelligence.

blocks.html_en:
I don't know how you can read my comment, not respond to my comment saying that today's self-driving cars use LIDAR, and continue to reiterate your point.

I don't think I was clear and explicit, it being tedious to write, and I apologize for that. I also apologize for shifting the goalposts as I had not written out my own position, which is not exactly in the "grandparent commenter"'s position (that I had not previously given enough attention understanding), but it is also not in agreement with yours. I don't mean to say that we are not presently in the "bitter lesson" (your idea of what the bitter lesson says) regime. I definitely think that a lot of progress can be done right now by emphasizing the humanoid robotics platform as a foundation. What I mean to say is that I don't know if that platform with the hardware we have today is sufficient for parity with human housekeeping tasks in the domains that we wish it to have parity. The bitter lesson itself (not your understanding of it) is in fact silent on this as it is in relation to feature engineering, where it is a clear point, but you seem to be adapting it uncritically wholesale to mean something more than what it is written about. My position is that, it is unclear whether today's sensor platform is sufficient for parity. It is less strong than the blog post author's "Why Today’s Humanoids Won’t Learn", it is a "We can't say whether or not today's humanoids will learn", but it is something that also contradicts a "the bitter lesson means today's humanoids will learn" thesis.

The self-driving car supports my claim, because after so much investment in capital and time, we ended up with a car with comparatively expensive LIDAR sensors as our preferred platform.

I also apologize for shifting the goalposts as I had not written out my own position, which is not exactly in the "grandparent commenter"'s position (that I had not previously given enough attention understanding), but it is also not in agreement with yours. I don't mean to say that we are not presently in the "bitter lesson" (your idea of what the bitter lesson says) regime. I definitely think that a lot of progress can be done right now by emphasizing the humanoid robotics platform as a foundation. What I mean to say is that I don't know if that platform with the hardware we have today is sufficient for parity with human housekeeping tasks in the domains that we wish it to have parity. The bitter lesson itself (not your understanding of it) is in fact silent on this as it is in relation to feature engineering, where it is a clear point, but you seem to be adapting it uncritically wholesale to mean something more than what it is written about. My position is that, it is unclear whether today's sensor platform is sufficient for parity. It is less strong than the blog post author's "Why Today’s Humanoids Won’t Learn", it is a "We can't say whether or not today's humanoids will learn", but it is something that also contradicts a "the bitter lesson means today's humanoids will learn" thesis.

The self-driving car supports my claim, because after so much investment in capital and time, we ended up with a car with comparatively expensive LIDAR sensors as our preferred platform.

blocks.html_en:
Tesla's entire fleet runs on raw cameras. Including the driverless Robotaxi vehicles - which are basically a 1:1 match to how Waymo operates.

Plenty of hecklers were saying "you can't self-drive on cameras", and some still try. But Tesla's self-driving on cameras, and it seems to work fine. While Waymo's self-driving on fat sensor stacks, and it also seems to work fine. Sensors don't seem to be a differentiator of self-driving performance.

I don't think anything about self-driving tech supports your claim. Tesla was bullish on AI all the way, and Waymo has also shifted towards highly integrated end to end AI. It's the AI advances that make self-driving tractable - not anything else.

blocks.html_en:
> political commentary from someone

No it depends on what they choose to answer. canyon289's account self-describes as Bayesian, a hallmark of rationalists, one of whose taglines is "politics is the mind-killer". Nonetheless https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/iKm2FhpWkuuBojm82/why-i-left... is one of the most upvoted posts on LessWrong (the big rationalist site) of all time. Most of the comments don't touch on the politics of the situation at all.

> someone just going about their job

They're doing a little bit more than that by actively recruiting (even more so than the usual "if this interests you we're hiring" bit at the end of a post). So I'm doing a little bit more by asking them about a recent high profile departure. It's a little bit different from the usual way employees chime in on threads.

Hey Ravin, I’m executive director for AGI Society which has run the AGI conference (https://agi-conference.org/) since 2007

We’d love to invite you to speak about your work next year at the AGI Conference if you’re open to it.

I’ll reach out on email if you have a preferred one, it was unclear on your site which email you prefer.

Working there feels like a trap.

Why work there when you can start a company? You get to choose the problem you care about most, the people you work with, and your own pace—and if it works, you own the success.

Margins means exactly what the poster you are replying to implies: that in the US Tesla has high margins (the difference between cost of good sold and what you get for them) because tarrifs make Chinese brands uncompetitive.

And as Tesla's latest financials showed they are under margin pressure too, even with that: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/tesla-tsla...

> in markets where BYD Sealion is sold - including China - Tesla Model Y outsells it!

Sure, but that's because BYD (for example) has both the Atto 3 and the Sealion which overlap in market segment.

content_html_zh: 虽然人择和开放人工智能在这里获得了 80% 的关注，但谷歌所做的努力令人印象深刻：近前沿模型、快速模型、开放权重模型、图像生成、视频生成、音乐生成、机器人技术等。这当然是一种奇怪的情况，谷歌处于所有这些新兴技术的最前沿，而来自 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的最新聊天机器人却得到了令人窒息的新闻稿和极度夸张的报道（“流氓人工智能”“太危险了，必须被禁止”等……）谷歌表现得像一家正常但有能力的公司，只是在缓慢发展，与此同时，炒作周期正在支撑其新兴竞争对手达到真正可笑的估值。> 谷歌表现得像一家正常但有能力的公司，只是在缓慢地前进。有能力是一种延伸。 谷歌的人工智能产品似乎再次由产品经理主导——许多不断变化的品牌被合并和弃用，客户支持或服务为零。他们几乎肯定会成为幸存者之一。 他们的技术能力是无与伦比的。 但这并不意味着他们拥有 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 那样的出色产品。 （在他们的数据中心之外，这是一个合法的壮举。）谷歌向来不擅长支持开发者，而且绝对厌恶最终用户。 对不属于他们的广告生态系统的一切的支持是悲惨的。 从来没有任何长期计划，一切都会被弃用并被淘汰。太疯狂了，他们一度拥有 3 个不同的系统来与 Gemini 交互，并且都具有不同的身份验证。对于一家以最聪明的工程师而自豪的公司来说，他们真的很难掌握基础知识嗯，然而，我对这个世界的体验越多，我就越发现这与帖子上的描述相符：> 谷歌表现得像一家正常但有能力的公司，它混乱而奇怪吗？ 是的。 不过还是很正常。 更糟糕的是，这与我在许多其他地方找到的能力基线相匹配。> 谷歌表现得像一家正常但有能力的公司，只是在不断地前进，不发布产品或发布比竞争对手更差的产品。 不确定这是一个正常的有能力的公司应该做的事情。> 谷歌表现得像一家正常但有能力的公司我只是在等待 10 个人工智能模型或聊天机器人应用程序像 10 个信使应用程序一样相互竞争。等待？ 你在说什么？ 我们已经被它们淹没了。 实际上，不仅仅是 Google Messenger 应用程序。 目前在线的 Google AI 聊天机器人的不完整列表： Gemini Gemini Live Gemini Code Assist Gemini for Google Cloud NotebookLM Gmail Google Docs Google Sheets Google Slides Google Drive Google Chat Google Meet Google Calendar Google Forms Google Vids AppSheet Workspace Studio Google Search Google app Google Chrome Google Lens Google Maps Google Flights Google Hotels Google Shopping Google Photos YouTube Google Messages Google Translate Android Circle to Search Google Home Google Play Pixel 应用程序和功能 Google Flow Google AI StudioGoogle 在基础设施和创造力（NotebookLM 等）方面获胜，但完全缺乏产品一致性。 这个生态系统是一团糟，就像微软的产品一样，我不认为这是巧合，而是这两家公司发展的公司类型的症状。此外，出于多种原因，Gemini 围绕着一种不太值得信赖和成熟的模式。 非常聪明，但在 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的最新模型中缺乏精确度和整体展示。 另一方面，谷歌在 Gemma 上的工作是无与伦比的。是的，令我惊讶的是我什至无法向 Gemini 添加自定义 MCP。 它有大量缺失的功能。我可以说肖像看起来不像一个人，即使我不能做得更好，谷歌的产品系列绝对是一团糟，使用它是一场噩梦——我不知道如何修复公司，但我知道结果很糟糕。在我第一次开始在微软商店工作之前，我一直认为谷歌是一团糟。 男孩，这太令人惊讶了。 我的计算机上有两个版本的 Outlook，它们的加载速度都不如 20 年前的 Thunderbird 快。 我的团队将 Azure DevOps 用于我们的 git forge，这在某种程度上是与 GitHub 完全不同的产品。 Teams 中有多个版本的 Planner，其中免费版本的功能并不是高级版本的严格子集 - 如果您付费，有些功能就会被屏蔽。 Google 吸引我的原因是，他们已经取消了太多我每天使用的产品（RIP Inbox 和 Google Podcasts），让我无法相信任何新产品都会在 5 年内出现。“我还发现我有两个 Microsoft Outlook，但如果您想远程登录并检查，则其中任何一个都无法工作”Cdr. 里德·怀斯曼 (Reid Wiseman) 前往阿耳忒弥斯二号地月海岸任务控制中心。我的意思是，他们实际上发明了法学硕士和许多现代机器学习的东西。 或者我应该说谷歌的研究人员。 他们会坚持下去是有道理的因为他们的产品实在是太差了。 上次我尝试 Gemini 时，当明确要求执行互联网搜索时，它反复撒谎。 我非常了解他们的模型基准测试，但在现实世界中，性能非常糟糕。> 谷歌表现得像一家正常但有能力的公司，只是在快速前进人们很快就忘记了几年前在他们的生成人工智能工作中出现的种族多元化的纳粹士兵和其他滑稽无能的东西。 谷歌看起来他们终于在巨大的竞争压力下团结起来，但在开始称他们为“有能力”之前，我会再关注他们几年。是的，我很惊讶没有人谈论 Gemini 应用程序中的“直播”功能。 打开相机后，它帮助我解决了我不知道的事情。谷歌 DeepMind 处于人工智能的最前沿，他们目前正在开发新概念，而其他人则在追逐基准百分比。这基本上是因为法学硕士取代了所有这些。 推理、研究和编写代码的能力适用于其他一切，并将显着加快创新周期。谷歌在真正重要的竞争中失败了我不会对此发表太多评论，但我想说这些文章晚了 2-3 年，降低了人们的代理性，在很多情况下，他们搬到双子座是因为他们想攻读法学硕士还有阿尔法狗零.. 这可能是现实世界中第一个击败人类的自我改进系统的部署。> 可能是现实世界中第一个击败人类的自我改进系统。这不是强化学习诞生之初的跳棋吗？这是一个巨大的进步，但它并没有击败世界冠军。 AlphaGo 因其自学系统而闻名，其表现优于所有人类。 国际象棋引擎早已存在，但在 AlphaZero 之前并不能自学习。我建议阅读 Sebastian Mallaby 的《无限机器：Demis Hassabis、DeepMind 和对超级智能的探索》。 它让您详细了解 Google/DeepMind 和其他前沿实验室的观察背后的原因。 迄今为止我在假期中读过的最好的书。事实是，谷歌有放弃支持或干脆终止项目的记录。 就我个人而言，我将谷歌的大部分产品和服务视为商业风险，因为你永远不知道它们什么时候会杀死它。虽然我同意，但很难相信谷歌将来不会取消这一功能。 他们没有获胜，并且放弃自己的公司而与另一家人工智能公司合作的前景也并非不可能。药物发现的瓶颈不是想出新分子等。而是需要多年、极其昂贵的临床试验，而且往往甚至不会成功。 我怀疑这对 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 来说会是一大笔钱，因为他们最大的希望就是向制药公司出售软件产品，但制药公司已经有很多科学家正在研究一百万个有前途的分子，他们甚至永远不会进入临床试验。换句话说，人工智能技术能提供帮助吗？ 也许吧，但我怀疑它会成为一个主要的赚钱工具，而且它不会在一夜之间赚很多钱。 它不像 Claude Code 那样每个程序员都可以立即开始使用它。如果你在 3 年前问 HN 代码生成市场会是什么样，他们会使用完全相同的推理并向我们给出这样的观点：“为什么没有人会为美化的自动完成付费”与科技公司正在做的事情并行的是，制药公司正在用人工智能审查取代临床试验。 我不太确定这是同一件事。人工智能治愈癌症、心脏病、衰老（你懂的）的想法不会赚钱，因为“临床试验”是荒谬的。 当然会。 显然它与编码代理不是一回事。 但很多赚钱者与编码代理并不相同。为了用人工智能治愈癌症，你需要让它完全控制实验流程，包括可能由机器人直接访问网络实验室，这有其自身的风险。 这与编码根本不是同一个问题空间。人们将会惊讶于几年后两者将获得多么可观的利润如果这最终是真的，他们应该感到非常惊讶。我们预计 2026 年超大规模资本支出将达到约 725B 美元（到 2028 年将达到 1.08T 美元），而 2025 年人工智能服务收入约为
